title: Cookies for the Guests
passage:
When Maha's mother announced that relatives from Riyadh would be visiting on Friday, Maha immediately volunteered to bake something special. There was only one serious difficulty: she had never baked anything independently before.

"Start with something uncomplicated," her mother advised, handing her a worn notebook full of handwritten recipes. Maha chose her grandmother's date cookies, known as maamoul, because everyone in the family praised them.

Her first attempt was a complete disaster, because she forgot to measure the semolina accurately and the dough crumbled into a sandy pile on the kitchen counter. Her second batch looked better, but she left the tray in the oven too long, and the cookies emerged hard and dark brown.

Maha felt completely discouraged and was ready to abandon the whole project. "Maybe baking simply isn't my talent," she sighed, staring at the burnt cookies.

Her mother sat beside her patiently. "Your grandmother burned her first batches too," she said with a smile. "Baking teaches you to be careful and patient."

On Thursday evening, Maha tried again. This time she measured every ingredient precisely, softened the dates carefully, and set a timer on her phone. As the sweet smell of butter and cardamom filled the kitchen, her confidence grew.

On Friday afternoon, the guests arrived, and Maha nervously offered them her golden cookies with Arabic coffee. Her aunt tasted one and closed her eyes. "These taste exactly like your grandmother's!" she exclaimed. Maha beamed with pride.

questions.stem: Which word from the story is an ADVERB?
options: golden
recipes
patiently
beamed
questions.why: 'Patiently' tells how her mother sat, so it is an adverb.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the word 'precisely' correctly?
options: She measured the flour precisely.
The precisely cookies were golden.
Maha precisely her aunt at the door.
He ate a precisely with his tea.
questions.why: 'Precisely' is an adverb meaning exactly; only this sentence uses it to describe an action.

questions.stem: Why did Maha choose to bake maamoul?
options: They were the quickest recipe to make
Everyone in the family praised them
Her aunt had asked for them by name
She had baked them many times before
questions.why: The story says she chose them 'because everyone in the family praised them.'

questions.stem: What happened right AFTER Maha's second batch came out hard and dark?
options: The dough crumbled into a sandy pile
Her mother gave her the recipe notebook
Her aunt tasted one of the cookies
She felt discouraged and wanted to quit
questions.why: After the burnt batch, 'Maha felt completely discouraged and was ready to abandon the whole project.'

questions.stem: How was Maha's last attempt different from her first two?
options: She followed her aunt's recipe instead
She measured carefully and used a timer
She baked them at her neighbor's house
She added extra semolina to the dough
questions.why: On Thursday 'she measured every ingredient precisely… and set a timer on her phone.'

questions.stem: 'Maha beamed with pride.' What does the word 'beamed' suggest?
options: She shone a light at the guests
She quickly left the room
She smiled widely and happily
She felt nervous and shy
questions.why: 'Beamed' means smiled brightly, like a beam of light.

questions.stem: What is the main message the writer wants to share?
options: Patience and practice lead to success
Guests only care about expensive food
Only adults can learn to bake well
Buying cookies is better than baking
questions.why: Maha fails twice but succeeds by being careful and patient, as her mother advised.

questions.stem: Which information in the story is LEAST complete?
options: Which recipe Maha decided to bake
What went wrong with her first batch
Why her second batch became hard
How many relatives visited on Friday
questions.why: The story only says 'relatives from Riyadh' without saying how many came.

options: Cookies bake themselves when a timer rings
Cookies left too long in an oven turn hard
Dough turns into real sand on a counter
A notebook reads its recipes out loud
questions.why: Overbaking makes cookies hard and dark, as in the story.

questions.stem: Which title BEST describes the events of the story?
options: The Guests Who Never Came
A Long Trip to Riyadh
Third Time Lucky
The Broken Oven
questions.why: Maha succeeds on her third attempt, after two failures.
